relations.subject: John Brough
relations.evidence: He then studied classics at St John's College, Cambridge, completing part 2 of the Tripos in 1940 (placing in the first-class) and then studying for the oriental languages Tripos, in part 2 of which he also placed in the first-class in 1942

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.evidence: Among his teachers was Sir Harold Bailey.

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.evidence: His efforts saw him awarded the DLitt from the University of Edinburgh in 1945.

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.object: Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum
relations.evidence: appointed (1944) assistant keeper in the Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum. Alongside that post, he was also a research fellow at St John's College, Cambridge, for a year from 1945 to 1946. In 1946, Brough left his post at the British Museum

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.evidence: he was also a research fellow at St John's College, Cambridge, for a year from 1945 to 1946.

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies in the University of London
relations.evidence: appointed to a lectureship in Sanskrit at the School of Oriental and African Studies in the University of London. Two years later, he was appointed to the second Professorship of Sanskrit in the University of London.

relations.subject: John Brough
relations.evidence: He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1948–67)

relations.evidence: He was also head of the Department of India, Pakistan and Ceylon in succession to Seymour Vesey-Fitzgerald.
